pilot.summary: Game four of four at Alex's house in Orinda, three-player with Alex and Stuart, and the one win of the night. I ramped through the early removal and the table spent its wipes on my mid-tier dinosaurs, which let me rebuild faster than they could answer — and meant that with my own board empty, Blasphemous Act cleared theirs at no cost to me. Then Gishath swung at Stuart for 7 and revealed five dinosaurs off the trigger, one of which made their creatures enter tapped. Next turn Enlarge made it a 14-point swing into 7 already dealt, lethal by commander damage, with two more dinosaurs off the second trigger. No changes to the deck.

Game two of two at Alex's, four-player: me, Alex on Azorius counters, Oliver on Vito, Tom on Aloro life gain, two and a half to three hours of wipe after wipe. Turn one was land, Sol Ring, Arcane Signet for four mana, then a long green screw with double-green dinos, Selvala and Rishkar's Expertise stuck in hand, which by accident kept my creatures off the table through the early wipe waves. Once green arrived Gishath came online, pumped and doubled to 16/16, and killed Tom with 16 commander damage on top of the 7 he had already taken; I broke a no-attack deal with Oliver to do it, because Tom's board would have wiped me otherwise, and I stand by that. Zakama off the Urza's Incubator discount and a well-timed Swords to Plowshares had the game effectively won, and then with 8 or 9 dinos, 30-plus power on board, Alex at 18 and Oliver at 15, I attacked only Oliver instead of both; Alex saved him and Oliver drained me out.

read.what_it_does: Two games logged, one on each list. What both show is a deck that ramps early and then waits on the commander: the kill each time was Gishath connecting for commander damage, not the dinosaurs in front of it. On V3 that was a swing of 7 at Stuart revealing five dinosaurs, then Enlarge for 14 into the 7 already dealt (001, on V3). On the sleeved list it was Gishath pumped and doubled to 16/16 killing Tom outright on top of the 7 he had taken, revealing two more dinosaurs off 16 cards (002). The bodies before Gishath went out and soaked the table's wipes in 001 and stayed in hand through the wipe waves in 002; either way the wraths were spent before the commander landed (001, 002).
read.how_it_plays: Slow and loud once it starts. Game 002 was two and a half to three hours of wipe after wipe in a four-player pod, with a turn-one Sol Ring and Arcane Signet and then a long stall while green arrived (002). When Gishath does connect it is a commander-damage kill in one or two swings, and the reveal restocks the board: five dinosaurs then two on V3 (001), two on the sleeved list with the board already stormed (002). It tends to end up with lethal on the board and a decision to make about who to swing at (002). The table treats it as a real threat afterwards, whether or not it won: Alex was salty in the morning text thread (002).
mindful_of: Close lethal when it is on the board. In 002 I had 8 or 9 dinos with counters and 30-plus power against Alex at 18 and Oliver at 15, should have swung everything at both so Alex saves himself and Oliver dies, and instead attacked only Oliver; Alex saved him and Oliver drained me out with a gain/lose/damage vampire spell. Hesitation cost the game (002).

Green. Turn one was four mana and I was still green-screwed for a long stretch with double-green dinos, Selvala and Rishkar's Expertise in hand (002). The green pip distribution and green sources in the mana base need an audit (002).
The enrage engine is idling: too few ping sources to activate it, and I read it as a better fit for Standard than Commander. The package is up for reconsideration (002).

Holding creatures back through wipe waves is a real strategy, not just an accident. It happened by accident in 002 and Gishath landed after the wraths were gone (002). On V3 the same result came the other way round, with mid-tier dinosaurs going out and soaking the removal until the commander arrived (001, on V3, before the six-swap check-in). Both games say the wraths have to be gone before Gishath is; which way to get there is the choice.
Blasphemous Act was one-sided only because my own board had already been answered (001, on V3). The card is still in the sleeved list and the condition still holds.

Deals. I had a no-attack deal with Oliver and broke it to kill Tom, because Tom's board would have wiped me otherwise, and I stand by it (002). The game is filed under politics: the loss came from Alex saving Oliver after I attacked only him (002).
Table standards. Alex claimed I should have announced the life-gain mode on Swords to Plowshares; that is not the table standard, and if he had a counter that was on him (002).

The V3 table spent its wraths on mid-tier dinosaurs and had nothing left for the commander (001, on V3). One game and one table; in 002 the same pod wiped repeatedly and my creatures were held back by the screw rather than misjudged (002). Do not count on a table misreading the threat twice.
read.what_changed: V3 to V4, the sleeved list, checked in 2026-09-11 as v1.0.0: Polyraptor, Forerunner of the Empire, Cultivate, Intrepid Paleontologist, Ranging Raptors and Ripjaw Raptor out; Earthshaker Dreadmaw, Enlarge, Kinjalli's Sunwing, Knight of the Stampede, Runic Armasaur and Sunfrill Imitator in. Game 001 was on V3 and I made no changes after it; the deck was working as designed (001). Game 002 is the first game on the sleeved list. Enlarge finished 001 and the debrief flagged that the tracked V3 did not hold it; the check-in put it in the 99, so the line that won 001 is one this list can draw (001, on V3). Cultivate left in the same check-in, and the follow-up from 002 is a green mana base audit; the note does not link the two and the audit is where that gets settled (002). The enrage package I want reconsidered after 002 is the one V4 holds, after Forerunner, Polyraptor, Ranging Raptors and Ripjaw Raptor had already gone (002). The tuning has moved from rebuilding the deck to sequencing and closing better: the change in direction after 002 is piloting, not the list, apart from the green audit and the enrage question (002).
